newsitem.title: USA: Josephine moving rapidly northeast to U.S. coast.
newsitem.headline: Josephine moving rapidly northeast to U.S. coast.

text.p: Tropical Storm Josephine continued moving rapidly toward the northeastern coast of the Gulf of Mexico Monday, prompting forecasters to post hurricane and tropical storm warnings for much of the Florida coast, the National Hurricane Center said.

At 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT), Josephine's center was near latitude 28.3 north and longitude 85.9 west, or about 110 miles (176 km) south-southwest of Apalachicola, Fla. It was moving northeast near 23 mph (37 kph).
"On this track the center of Jospehine will cross the coast in the hurricane warning area this evening," the National Hurricane Center said.

A hurricane warning is in effect from the Anclote Keys to Apalachicola, Fla. A tropical storm warning was in effect south of the Anclote Keys to Venice, Fla., and west of Apalachicaola to Fort Walton Beach, Fla.
A tropical storm warning was in effect for the U.S. east coast from Cape Canaveral, Fla., northward to Little River Inlet, S.C.
Maximum sustained winds were 70 mph (112 kph) and forecasters said Josephine could become a hurricane, with winds of at least 74 mph (119 kph), by landfall.
Tropical storm force winds extended outward up to 175 miles (280 km) from Josephine's center. Rainfall amounts of 5 inches (12.5 cm) or more were possible along the storm's path.
Strong onshore winds were expected to cause coastal storm surge flooding of 6 to 9 feet (2 to 3 meters) or higher near and to the south and east of where the storm's center came ashore.
